briefing.title: Briefing after cycle 014 — what the world is pressing on

question: Which of these two should the world act on first, in the coming year?

matters.title: Five companies, most of the machines
matters.gist: Five cloud companies own most of the world's computing power for AI, and governments are moving to control who may rent it.

matters.title: Interest before hospitals
matters.gist: In much of the developing world, governments now spend more on interest to creditors than on health or on education.

matters.title: Appeals less than half funded
matters.gist: With two months of the year left, the world's humanitarian appeals have received less than half of what they asked for.

matters.title: One in ten below three dollars a day
matters.gist: Extreme poverty barely moves: about one in ten people live on less than three dollars a day, rising in one region and high in another.

matters.title: A record of conflicts between states
matters.gist: Organised violence killed far more people in 2025 than the year before, in more conflicts between states than ever recorded.

matters.title: A fifth of those counted, in crisis
matters.gist: In the countries with food crises, more than a fifth of the people analysed could not reliably eat enough, and Congo now has a record number in crisis.

matters.title: Press freedom at a 25-year low
matters.gist: In more than half the world's countries, journalism now works under conditions rated difficult or very serious.

matters.title: More AI harms on record
matters.gist: The public record of harms caused by AI systems grew sharply in 2025, while young workers in exposed jobs fell behind.

matters.title: Ebola in Congo, still running
matters.gist: The Bundibugyo outbreak in eastern Congo is the country's largest, still at hundreds of cases a week six months on, with cases in Kenya and Nigeria.

matters.title: COP31 in its second week, on a 2.8-degree path
matters.gist: The climate summit in Antalya is drafting its outcome while current policies still point to far more warming than the Paris goal.
